claim: The V-ATPase is a versatile proton-pump found in a range of endomembrane compartments.
source: The V-ATPase is a versatile proton-pump found in a range of endomembrane compartments yet the mechanisms governing its differential targeting remain to be determined.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about V-ATPases being present in multiple cellular compartments.

claim: In Arabidopsis, VHA-a1 targets the V-ATPase to the TGN/EE.
source: In Arabidopsis, VHA-a1 targets the V-ATPase to the TGN/EE whereas VHA-a2 and VHA-a3 are localized to the tonoplast.
evidence: This is supported by previous work cited in the manuscript (Dettmer et al., 2006) and confirmed by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: VHA-a2 and VHA-a3 are localized to the tonoplast.
source: In Arabidopsis, VHA-a1 targets the V-ATPase to the TGN/EE whereas VHA-a2 and VHA-a3 are localized to the tonoplast.
evidence: This is supported by previous work (Dettmer et al., 2006) and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The VHA-a1 targeting domain serves as both an ER-exit and as a TGN/EE-retention motif.
source: We report here that the VHA-a1 targeting domain serves as both an ER-exit and as a TGN/EE-retention motif and is conserved among seed plants.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments with dominant negative Sar1 and site-directed mutagenesis shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The VHA-a1 targeting domain is conserved among seed plants.
source: We report here that the VHA-a1 targeting domain serves as both an ER-exit and as a TGN/EE-retention motif and is conserved among seed plants.
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis and functional complementation experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Marchantia encodes a single VHA-isoform that localizes to the TGN/EE and the tonoplast in Arabidopsis.
source: In contrast, Marchantia encodes a single VHA-isoform that localizes to the TGN/EE and the tonoplast in Arabidopsis.
evidence: This is demonstrated by localization experiments shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: VHA-a1 has an essential function for male gametophyte development.
source: Analysis of CRISPR/Cas9 generated null alleles revealed that VHA-a1 has an essential function for male gametophyte development but acts redundantly with the tonoplast isoforms during vegetative growth.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the pollen phenotype of vha-a1 mutants shown in Figure 9.

claim: VHA-a1 acts redundantly with the tonoplast isoforms during vegetative growth.
source: Analysis of CRISPR/Cas9 generated null alleles revealed that VHA-a1 has an essential function for male gametophyte development but acts redundantly with the tonoplast isoforms during vegetative growth.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the lack of vegetative phenotype in vha-a1 mutants and genetic crosses shown in Figure 9 and Figure 10.

claim: In the absence of VHA-a1, VHA-a3 is partially re-routed to the TGN/EE.
source: We propose that in the absence of VHA-a1, VHA-a3 is partially re-routed to the TGN/EE.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the observation that vha-a1 mutants are viable and show hypersensitivity to ConcA, suggesting V-ATPase activity at the TGN/EE.

claim: V-ATPases consist of two subcomplexes: The cytosolic V1 subcomplex and the membrane-integral VO subcomplex.
source: They consist of two subcomplexes: The cytosolic V1 subcomplex responsible for ATP hydrolysis composed of eight different subunits (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H) and the membrane-integral VO subcomplex consisting of 6 subunits (a, d, e, c, c', c') required for proton translocation (Sze et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about V-ATPase structure, supported by citation.

claim: The cytosolic V1 subcomplex is responsible for ATP hydrolysis and is composed of eight different subunits (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H).
source: They consist of two subcomplexes: The cytosolic V1 subcomplex responsible for ATP hydrolysis composed of eight different subunits (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H) and the membrane-integral VO subcomplex consisting of 6 subunits (a, d, e, c, c', c') required for proton translocation (Sze et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about V-ATPase structure, supported by citation.

claim: The membrane-integral VO subcomplex consists of 6 subunits (a, d, e, c, c', c') required for proton translocation.
source: They consist of two subcomplexes: The cytosolic V1 subcomplex responsible for ATP hydrolysis composed of eight different subunits (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H) and the membrane-integral VO subcomplex consisting of 6 subunits (a, d, e, c, c', c') required for proton translocation (Sze et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about V-ATPase structure, supported by citation.

claim: Differential targeting of the V-ATPase is mediated by isoforms of subunit a.
source: Differential targeting of the V-ATPase is mediated by isoforms of subunit a, the largest of the V-ATPase subunits that consists of a C- terminal hydrophobic domain with eight transmembrane domains and a large N-terminal domain that is accessible for cytosolic interaction partners (Zhao et al., 2015; Vasanthakumar et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations and is a central concept of the manuscript.

claim: Subunit a is the largest of the V-ATPase subunits.
source: Differential targeting of the V-ATPase is mediated by isoforms of subunit a, the largest of the V-ATPase subunits that consists of a C- terminal hydrophobic domain with eight transmembrane domains and a large N-terminal domain that is accessible for cytosolic interaction partners (Zhao et al., 2015; Vasanthakumar et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Subunit a consists of a C-terminal hydrophobic domain with eight transmembrane domains and a large N-terminal domain that is accessible for cytosolic interaction partners.
source: Differential targeting of the V-ATPase is mediated by isoforms of subunit a, the largest of the V-ATPase subunits that consists of a C- terminal hydrophobic domain with eight transmembrane domains and a large N-terminal domain that is accessible for cytosolic interaction partners (Zhao et al., 2015; Vasanthakumar et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about subunit a structure, supported by citations.

claim: The targeting information is contained in the N-terminal domain of subunit a.
source: Previous studies in yeast and plants have shown that the targeting information is contained in the N-terminal domain (Dettmer et al., 2006; Kawasaki-Nishi et al., 2001a), however the responsible targeting domain has so far only been addressed for the yeast isoforms Vhp1p and Stv1p.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vph1p targets the yeast V-ATPase to the vacuole.
source: Whereas Vph1p targets the yeast V-ATPase to the vacuole, a motif containing an aromatic residue (WKY) in the N-terminus of Stv1p targets the V-ATPase to the Golgi/endosomal network (Finnigan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about yeast V-ATPase targeting, supported by citation.

claim: A motif containing an aromatic residue (WKY) in the N-terminus of Stv1p targets the V-ATPase to the Golgi/endosomal network.
source: Whereas Vph1p targets the yeast V-ATPase to the vacuole, a motif containing an aromatic residue (WKY) in the N-terminus of Stv1p targets the V-ATPase to the Golgi/endosomal network (Finnigan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about yeast V-ATPase targeting, supported by citation.

claim: The localization of Stv1p at the Golgi is dependent on interaction of the WKY motif with phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate (PI(4)P).
source: The localization of Stv1p at the Golgi is dependent on interaction of the WKY motif with phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate (PI(4)P; Banerjee and Kane, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Mammals possess four subunit a isoforms (a1, a2, a3, and a4) which steer the V-ATPase to different endomembranes or the plasma membrane.
source: Mammals possess four subunit a isoforms (a1, a2, a3, and a4) which steer the V-ATPase to different endomembranes or the plasma membrane (Forgac, 2007; Marshansky et al., 2014; Futai et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian V-ATPase isoforms, supported by citations.

claim: VHA-a2 and VHA-a3 target the V-ATPase to the tonoplast where the combined action of V-ATPase and V-PPase energizes secondary active transport and maintains the acidic environment required for the lytic function of plant vacuoles.
source: In Arabidopsis VHA-a2 and VHA-a3 target the V-ATPase to the tonoplast (Dettmer et al., 2006) where the combined action of V-ATPase and V-PPase energizes secondary active transport and maintains the acidic environment required for the lytic function of plant vacuoles (Sze et al., 1999; Kriegel et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: VHA-a1 targets the V-ATPase to the TGN/EE, a highly dynamic organelle that receives and sorts proteins from the endocytic, recycling and secretory pathways.
source: In contrast, VHA-a1 targets the V-ATPase to the TGN/EE, a highly dynamic organelle that receives and sorts proteins from the endocytic, recycling and secretory pathways (Dettmer et al., 2006; Viotti et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The combined action of the V-ATPase and proton-coupled antiporters including the NHX-type cation proton exchangers and the ClC Cl-/NO- proton antiporters is responsible for generating and maintaining the acidic pH of the TGN/EE.
source: The combined action of the V-ATPase and proton-coupled antiporters including the NHX-type cation proton exchangers (Bassil et al., 2011a and Bassil et al., 2011b; Dragwidge et al., 2019) and the ClC (Chloride channel) Cl-/NO- proton antiporters (von der Fecht-Bartenbach et al., 2007) is responsible for generating and maintaining the acidic pH of the TGN/EE (Luo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of the V-ATPase interferes with endocytic and secretory trafficking.
source: Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of the V-ATPase interferes with endocytic and secretory trafficking (Dettmer et al., 2006; Viotti et al., 2010; Luo et al., 2015) and causes defects in both cell division and cell expansion (Dettmer et al., 2006; Brüx et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of the V-ATPase causes defects in both cell division and cell expansion.
source: Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of the V-ATPase interferes with endocytic and secretory trafficking (Dettmer et al., 2006; Viotti et al., 2010; Luo et al., 2015) and causes defects in both cell division and cell expansion (Dettmer et al., 2006; Brüx et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 containing Vo-subcomplexes leave the ER via different trafficking routes.
source: We have shown previously that after assembly involving dedicated ER-chaperones (Neubert et al., 2008), VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 containing Vo-subcomplexes leave the ER via different trafficking routes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: VHA-a1 containing V-ATPases are exported in a coat protein complex II (COPII)-dependent manner.
source: Whereas VHA-a1 containing V-ATPases are exported in a coat protein complex II (COPII)-dependent manner (Viotti et al., 2013), VHA-a3 containing complexes have been shown to be delivered in a Golgi-independent manner to the tonoplast (Viotti et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and confirmed by experiments in Figure 3.

claim: VHA-a3 containing complexes have been shown to be delivered in a Golgi-independent manner to the tonoplast.
source: Whereas VHA-a1 containing V-ATPases are exported in a coat protein complex II (COPII)-dependent manner (Viotti et al., 2013), VHA-a3 containing complexes have been shown to be delivered in a Golgi-independent manner to the tonoplast (Viotti et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Targeting of TGN-resident proteins has been shown to be mediated by groups of acidic amino acids (acidic clusters), di-leucine and tyrosine-based motifs in mammals.
source: Targeting of TGN-resident proteins has been shown to be mediated by groups of acidic amino acids (acidic clusters), di-leucine and tyrosine-based motifs in mammals (Bos et al., 1993; Schäfer et al., 1995; Alconada et al., 1996; Xiang et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge about TGN targeting in mammals, supported by citations.

claim: In yeast, retrieval to the late Golgi is dependent on the concerted action of aromatic-based amino acid motifs in the cytoplasmic tails of proteins and slow anterograde transport to the late endosome.
source: In yeast, retrieval to the late Golgi (equivalent to the TGN) is dependent on the concerted action of aromatic-based amino acid (aa) motifs in the cytoplasmic tails of proteins and slow anterograde transport to the late endosome (Wilcox et al., 1992; Nothwehr et al., 1993; Cooper and Stevens, 1996; Cereghino et al., 1995; Bryant and Stevens, 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge about yeast Golgi targeting, supported by citations.

claim: The TGN/EE targeting information is contained within the first 228 aa of VHA-a1.
source: We have previously shown that the TGN/EE targeting information is contained within the first 228 aa of VHA-a1 (Dettmer et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The tri-peptide motif that mediates Golgi-localization of Stv1p in yeast is not conserved in VHA-a1.
source: The tri-peptide motif that mediates Golgi-localization of Stv1p in yeast (Finnigan et al., 2012) is not conserved in VHA-a1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) implying that TGN/EE localization evolved independently.
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: TGN/EE localization evolved independently in plants compared to yeast.
source: The tri-peptide motif that mediates Golgi-localization of Stv1p in yeast (Finnigan et al., 2012) is not conserved in VHA-a1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) implying that TGN/EE localization evolved independently.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of conservation of the yeast targeting motif in VHA-a1.

claim: a1NT37a3-GFP localizes to the tonoplast.
source: Whereas a1NT37a3-GFP, a1NT85a3-GFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and a1NT131a3-GFP (Figure 1A) all localized to the tonoplast, a1NT179a3-GFP and a1NT228a3-GFP were detectable at the tonoplast but also in a punctate pattern reminiscent of the TGN/EE (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: a1NT85a3-GFP localizes to the tonoplast.
source: Whereas a1NT37a3-GFP, a1NT85a3-GFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and a1NT131a3-GFP (Figure 1A) all localized to the tonoplast, a1NT179a3-GFP and a1NT228a3-GFP were detectable at the tonoplast but also in a punctate pattern reminiscent of the TGN/EE (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: a1NT131a3-GFP localizes to the tonoplast.
source: Whereas a1NT37a3-GFP, a1NT85a3-GFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and a1NT131a3-GFP (Figure 1A) all localized to the tonoplast, a1NT179a3-GFP and a1NT228a3-GFP were detectable at the tonoplast but also in a punctate pattern reminiscent of the TGN/EE (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 1A.

claim: a1NT179a3-GFP and a1NT228a3-GFP were detectable at the tonoplast but also in a punctate pattern reminiscent of the TGN/EE.
source: Whereas a1NT37a3-GFP, a1NT85a3-GFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and a1NT131a3-GFP (Figure 1A) all localized to the tonoplast, a1NT179a3-GFP and a1NT228a3-GFP were detectable at the tonoplast but also in a punctate pattern reminiscent of the TGN/EE (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 1A.

claim: TGN/EE localization of a1NT179a3-GFP and a1NT228a3-GFP was confirmed by colocalization with the endocytic tracer FM4-64.
source: TGN/EE localization was confirmed by colocalization with the endocytic tracer FM4-64 (Dettmer et al., 2006) and treatment with the fungal drug Brefeldin A (BFA) that causes the aggregation of the TGN/EE to form BFA compartments (Nebenführ et al., 2002; Dettmer et al., 2006).
evidence: This is demonstrated by colocalization experiments shown in Figure 1B.

claim: After 3 hr of BFA treatment, the core of BFA compartments was labeled by a1NT179a3-GFP and a1NT228a3-GFP.
source: After 3 hr of BFA treatment, the core of BFA compartments was labeled by a1NT179a3-GFP and a1NT228a3-GFP (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 1B.

claim: The region necessary for TGN/EE localization of VHA-a1 (a1-targeting domain; a1-TD) is located between residues L132 and E179.
source: From these observations, we concluded that the region necessary for TGN/EE localization of VHA-a1 (a1-targeting domain; a1-TD) is located between residues L132 and E179.
evidence: This is inferred from the localization patterns of chimeric proteins shown in Figure 1.

claim: The a1-TD is one of the regions predicted to be different between VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 N-termini.
source: Superimposition of the obtained models for the VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 N-termini revealed that the a1-TD is one of the regions predicted to be different (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by 3D homology modeling shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The a1-TD would be accessible for recognition in the fully assembled V-ATPase complex.
source: To visualize the orientation of the VHA-a1 N-terminus within the V-ATPase complex, we aligned our model for the VHA-a1 N-terminus model with the structure of the yeast V-ATPase (PDB6O7V; Vasanthakumar et al., 2019) and found that the a1-TD would be accessible for recognition in the fully assembled V-ATPase complex (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural alignment shown in Figure 1D.

claim: VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP is detectable at the tonoplast and at the TGN/EE where it colocalizes with VHA-a1-mRFP.
source: To test if the VHA-a1-TD is sufficient to target VHA‐a3 to the TGN/EE, we introduced the 34 aa region between K140 and S174 into the N-terminus of VHA-a3. The resulting GFP fusion construct (UBQ10:VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP) was transformed into wildtype plants and VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP was detectable at the tonoplast and at the TGN/EE where it colocalized with VHA-a1-mRFP (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 1E.

claim: The a1-TD is sufficient to partially re-route VHA-a3 to the TGN/EE.
source: It remains to be determined why TGN/EE localization of VHA-a3-a1-TD is only partial, however it demonstrates that the a1-TD is sufficient to partially re-route VHA-a3 to the TGN/EE.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the localization of VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP shown in Figure 1E.

claim: VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 represent two clearly separated clades in phylogenetic analysis of VHA-a sequences from mono- and dicot species.
source: Phylogenetic analysis of VHA-a sequences from mono- and dicot species showed that VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 represent two clearly separated clades (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The a1-TD includes a number of amino acids conserved among all of the sequences in the VHA-a1 clade but not in the VHA-a3 clade.
source: The a1-TD includes a number of amino acids conserved among all of the sequences in the VHA-a1 clade (Figure 2A) but not in the VHA-a3 clade that could either be part of a di-acidic ER-export motif or an acidic cluster involved in TGN/EE-retention.
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Mutations E161S and F134Y predominantly localized to the TGN/EE.
source: Mutations with high Pearson's correlation coefficients predominately localized to the TGN/EE (E161S and F134Y; Figure 2C,D and K).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy and colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mutations L159T + E161S, L159T, E155 + E156 + I157 deletion (ΔEEI) led to a dual TGN/EE and tonoplast localization.
source: Three mutations led to a dual TGN/EE and tonoplast localization (L159T + E161S, L159T, E155 + E156 + I157 deletion (ΔEEI) and Figure 2E,F,G and H) and had intermediate Pearson's and Mander's coefficients (M2) (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy and colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mutations E156Q and E156Q + L159T led to VHA-a1 being localized to an unknown compartment.
source: Two mutations led to VHA-a1 being localized to an unknown compartment (E156Q and E156Q + L159T; Figure 2I and J) and had the lowest Pearson's and Mander's coefficients (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy and colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Upon induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP, large clusters of vesicles in the periphery of Golgi stack remnants and ER cisternae appeared swollen.
source: Upon induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP, we observed large clusters of vesicles in the periphery of Golgi stack remnants and ER cisternae appeared swollen (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by electron microscopy images in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP caused ER-retention and colocalization with AtSar1b-GTP-CFP in bright and often large punctae for ST-GFP and BRI1-GFP.
source: Furthermore, in Arabidopsis transgenic lines expressing the Golgi-marker Sialyl transferase (ST; Boevink et al., 1998) or the brassinosteroid receptor (BRI1; Geldner et al., 2007) as GFP fusion proteins, induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP caused their ER-retention and colocalization with AtSar1b-GTP-CFP in bright and often large punctae that might represent the clusters of uncoated COPII vesicles as observed by EM (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The punctate pattern of VHA-a1-GFP disappeared after induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP and was replaced by a characteristic ER pattern with dense punctae that colocalized with AtSar1b-GTP-CFP.
source: Similarly, the punctate pattern of VHA-a1-GFP disappeared after induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP and was replaced by a characteristic ER pattern with dense punctae that colocalized with AtSar1b-GTP-CFP (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3A.

claim: VHA-a3-GFP was not retained in the ER after the induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP.
source: In contrast, VHA-a3-GFP was not retained in the ER after the induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3B.

claim: In cells in which VHA-a1-GFP was retained in the ER, VHA-a3-mRFP was not affected.
source: To exclude that these differences in ER retention between VHA-a1-GFP and VHA-a3-GFP were due to differences in induction strength of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP, we also blocked ER exit in a line co-expressing VHA-a1-GFP and VHA-a3-mRFP. In cells in which VHA-a1-GFP was retained in the ER, VHA-a3-mRFP was not affected (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3C.

claim: VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP is partially retained in the ER upon expression of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP.
source: Conversely, VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP is partially retained in the ER upon expression of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3D.

claim: The ER-export of VHA-a1 is COPII-dependent.
source: Taken together, our data confirms that the ER-export of VHA-a1 is COPII-dependent and reveals that the a1-TD contains an ER-export signal.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with dominant negative Sar1 shown in Figure 3.

claim: The a1-TD contains an ER-export signal.
source: Taken together, our data confirms that the ER-export of VHA-a1 is COPII-dependent and reveals that the a1-TD contains an ER-export signal.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with dominant negative Sar1 and VHA-a3-a1-TD shown in Figure 3.

claim: Blocking ER-export causes an increase in the trafficking to the tonoplast via a Golgi-independent route for mutated VHA-a1 proteins.
source: When AtSar1b-GTP was used to block ER exit, we observed a significant increase in the GFP fluorescence intensity at the tonoplast for all the mutated VHA-a1 proteins (Figure 4A and B) indicating that blocking ER-export causes an increase in the trafficking to the tonoplast via a Golgi-independent route.
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 4.

claim: When the mutated VHA-a1 proteins were expressed in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant, the ratio of TGN/EE-to-tonoplast fluorescence intensity increased as compared to the wildtype background.
source: Indeed, when the mutated VHA-a1 proteins were expressed in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant, the ratio of TGN/EE-to-tonoplast fluorescence intensity increased as compared to the wildtype background (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 5.

claim: VHA-a1 mutants that showed only TGN localization (E161S) or a punctate pattern that is different from VHA-a1-RFP (E156Q and E156Q+ L159T) in the wildtype background displayed a tonoplast signal in the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant.
source: Similarly, VHA-a1 mutants that showed only TGN localization (E161S) or a punctate pattern that is different from VHA-a1-RFP (E156Q and E156Q+ L159T) in the wildtype background displayed a tonoplast signal in the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 5A.

claim: All mutations affect ER export and the observed tonoplast signal is not a result of poor retention at the TGN/EE but due to a Golgi-independent pathway to the tonoplast.
source: These results strongly support the idea that all mutations affect ER export and that the observed tonoplast signal is not a result of poor retention at the TGN/EE but due to a Golgi-independent pathway to the tonoplast.
evidence: This is inferred from the results shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: All VHA-a isoforms from seed plants including the gymnosperm Pinus taeda cluster into two distinct clades containing VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 respectively.
source: Our analysis revealed that all VHA-a isoforms from seed plants including the gymnosperm Pinus taeda cluster into two distinct clades containing VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 respectively (Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6A.

claim: The genomes of most basal plants encode multiple isoforms of VHA-a, however they do not fall into either of the VHA-a1 or VHA-a3 clades implying that duplication of VHA-a occurred independently.
source: Interestingly, the genomes of most basal plants encode multiple isoforms of VHA-a, however they do not fall into either of these two clades implying that duplication of VHA-a occurred independently.
evidence: This is inferred from phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The hallmarks of the a1-TD (acidic residues flanking a critical leucine residue) are conserved throughout the angiosperms but are absent in bryophytes, lycophytes, ferns and hornworts.
source: Closer analysis of the a1-TD sequence revealed that the hallmarks of the a1-TD (acidic residues flanking a critical leucine residue) are conserved throughout the angiosperms but are absent in bryophytes, lycophytes, ferns and hornworts.
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The gymnosperm sequence from P. taeda contains the a1-TD sequence with the exception of one flanking glutamic residue.
source: Interestingly, the gymnosperm sequence from P. taeda contains the a1-TD sequence with the exception of one flanking glutamic residue (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The Pine and Amborella chimeric proteins colocalized with VHA-a1 at the TGN/EE.
source: Whereas the Pine and Amborella chimeric proteins colocalized with VHA-a1 at the TGN/EE, the Selaginella chimeric protein localized to the tonoplast.
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 6C.

claim: The Selaginella chimeric protein localized to the tonoplast.
source: Whereas the Pine and Amborella chimeric proteins colocalized with VHA-a1 at the TGN/EE, the Selaginella chimeric protein localized to the tonoplast.
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 6C.

claim: The a1-TD domain is conserved within the spermatophytes but not in other green plants.
source: These results suggest that the a1-TD domain is conserved within the spermatophytes but not in other green plants.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional complementation experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Complementation of the dwarfed phenotype of the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant correlated with the intensity of the tonoplast signal.
source: We confirmed that the proteins were expressed (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) and observed that complementation of the growth phenotype correlated with the intensity of the tonoplast signal with VHA-a1E161S-GFP conferring the lowest and VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP the highest degree of rescue (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area measurements and localization data shown in Figure 7.

claim: VHA-a1E161S-GFP conferred the lowest degree of rescue of the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant.
source: We confirmed that the proteins were expressed (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) and observed that complementation of the growth phenotype correlated with the intensity of the tonoplast signal with VHA-a1E161S-GFP conferring the lowest and VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP the highest degree of rescue (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area measurements shown in Figure 7.

claim: VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP conferred the highest degree of rescue of the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant.
source: We confirmed that the proteins were expressed (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) and observed that complementation of the growth phenotype correlated with the intensity of the tonoplast signal with VHA-a1E161S-GFP conferring the lowest and VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP the highest degree of rescue (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area measurements shown in Figure 7.

claim: All VHA-a1-GFP mutation lines had more acidic vacuoles than the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant but none of them reached wildtype vacuolar pH.
source: Whereas all VHA-a1-GFP mutation lines had more acidic vacuoles than the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant none of them reached wildtype vacuolar pH (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell sap pH measurements shown in Figure 7C.

claim: VHA-a1 containing complexes are functional when mistargeted to the tonoplast but their enzymatic properties are different and they cannot fully replace the vacuolar isoforms.
source: Taken together, our data indicates that although VHA-a1 containing complexes are functional when mistargeted to the tonoplast their enzymatic properties are different and they cannot fully replace the vacuolar isoforms.
evidence: This is inferred from the complementation and pH measurement data shown in Figure 7.

claim: MpVHA-a-mVenus driven by the CaMV35S or MpEF1α promoter predominantly localized to the vacuolar membrane, but some additional punctate structures were detectable.
source: MpVHA-a-mVenus driven by the CaMV35S or MpEF1α promoter predominantly localized to the vacuolar membrane, but some additional punctate structures were detectable (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: MpVHA-a-mVenus localization at the tonoplast of root cells was clearly visible.
source: Next, we expressed a MpVHA-a-mVenus fusion construct (UBQ10:MpVHA-a-mVenus) in the Arabidopsis wildtype background. Whereas MpVHA-a-mVenus localization at the tonoplast of root cells was clearly visible (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), a clear punctate pattern was not observed.
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: After BFA treatment, the core of BFA compartments was labeled with MpVHA-a-mVenus indicating that MpVHA-a is also present at the TGN/EE.
source: However, after BFA treatment, the core of BFA compartments was labeled with MpVHA-a-mVenus (Figure 8—figure supplement 2) indicating that MpVHA-a is also present at the TGN/EE.
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: MpVHA-a-mVenus localized to the TGN/EE and tonoplast and was found in the core of FM4-64 labeled BFA compartments in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant background.
source: To test for functionality, MpVHA-a-mVenus was expressed in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant background. MpVHA-a-mVenus localized to the TGN/EE and tonoplast and was found in the core of FM4-64 labeled BFA compartments (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 8A.

claim: V-ATPases that incorporate MpVHA-a can complement the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant to wildtype levels in terms of rosette size and cell sap pH.
source: A growth assay conducted in short day conditions (SD; 22 °C and 10 hr light) revealed that V-ATPases that incorporate MpVHA-a can complement the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant to wildtype levels in terms of rosette size and cell sap pH (Figure 8B and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area and cell sap pH measurements shown in Figure 8B and C.

claim: Homozygous and bi-allelic vha-a1 individuals were indistinguishable from wildtype during vegetative growth.
source: Surprisingly, we did not only identify heterozygous vha-a1/+ but also homozygous and bi-allelic vha-a1 individuals (Supplementary file 1). The latter two were indistinguishable from wildtype during vegetative growth (Figure 9B), but failed to produce seeds due to a defect in pollen development (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by plant images shown in Figure 9B.

claim: vha-a1 mutants failed to produce seeds due to a defect in pollen development.
source: Surprisingly, we did not only identify heterozygous vha-a1/+ but also homozygous and bi-allelic vha-a1 individuals (Supplementary file 1). The latter two were indistinguishable from wildtype during vegetative growth (Figure 9B), but failed to produce seeds due to a defect in pollen development (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by Alexander staining of pollen shown in Figure 9C.

claim: vha-a1 mutants expressing VHA-a1-GFP under the control of UBQ10 promoter showed normal pollen development.
source: Importantly, all plants with no wildtype allele of either VHA-a1 or VHA-a1-GFP were defective in pollen development, whereas vha-a1 mutants expressing VHA-a1-GFP under the control of UBQ10 promoter showed normal pollen development (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by Alexander staining of pollen shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Transmission of vha-a1-1 via the male gametophyte required the presence of VHA-a1-GFP.
source: As expected, vha-a1-1 was only transmitted via the male gametophyte in the presence of VHA-a1-GFP.
evidence: This is demonstrated by genetic crosses shown in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Transmission of vha-a1-1 via the female gametophyte did not require the presence of the transgene indicating that development of the female gametophyte is not affected.
source: In contrast, transmission of vha-a1-1 via the female gametophyte did not require the presence of the transgene indicating that development of the female gametophyte is not affected (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by genetic crosses shown in Supplementary file 1.

claim: MpVHA-a-mVenus did not rescue the pollen phenotype of vha-a1.
source: Using this strategy, we identified bi–allelic and homozygous vha-a1 mutants expressing UBQ10:MpVHA-a-mVenus and found that it was localized both at the TGN/EE and the tonoplast (Figure 9—figure supplement 2). However, MpVHA-a-mVenus did not rescue the pollen phenotype of vha-a1 (Figure 9—figure supplement 2) indicating that the TGN/EE-localized V-ATPase of seed plants has acquired a unique function during pollen development.
evidence: This is demonstrated by Alexander staining of pollen shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claim: The TGN/EE-localized V-ATPase of seed plants has acquired a unique function during pollen development.
source: Using this strategy, we identified bi–allelic and homozygous vha-a1 mutants expressing UBQ10:MpVHA-a-mVenus and found that it was localized both at the TGN/EE and the tonoplast (Figure 9—figure supplement 2). However, MpVHA-a-mVenus did not rescue the pollen phenotype of vha-a1 (Figure 9—figure supplement 2) indicating that the TGN/EE-localized V-ATPase of seed plants has acquired a unique function during pollen development.
evidence: This is inferred from the failure of MpVHA-a to rescue the pollen phenotype.

claim: vha-a1 is hypersensitive to the V-ATPase inhibitor Concanamycin-A (ConcA).
source: However, vha-a1 is hypersensitive to the V-ATPase inhibitor Concanamycin-A (ConcA).
evidence: This is demonstrated by hypocotyl length measurements shown in Figure 10A.

claim: vha-a1 vha-a1-GFP etiolated seedlings displayed shorter hypocotyls and had deformed roots in contrast to vha-a1 mutants expressing VHA-a1-GFP.
source: Analysis of the progeny of vha-a1 VHA-a1-GFP (Cas9+) mutants revealed that vha-a1 vha-a1-GFP etiolated seedlings displayed shorter hypocotyls and had deformed roots in contrast to vha-a1 mutants expressing VHA-a1-GFP.
evidence: This is demonstrated by hypocotyl length measurements and root morphology shown in Figure 10A and Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: A target of ConcA is present at the TGN/EE in vha-a1 albeit in small amounts or with a higher sensitivity to ConcA.
source: This result indicates that a target of ConcA is present at the TGN/EE in vha-a1 albeit in small amounts or with a higher sensitivity to ConcA. (Figure 10A and Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the hypersensitivity of vha-a1 to ConcA.

claim: vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ mutants were significantly smaller than vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ individuals indicating that tonoplast V-ATPases compensate for the lack of VHA-a1 during vegetative growth.
source: To test if VHA-a2 or VHA-a3-containing V-ATPases might compensate for the lack of VHA-a1, vha-a1-1 (Cas9+) was crossed with the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant. vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ mutants obtained from this cross were significantly smaller than vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ individuals indicating that tonoplast V-ATPases indeed compensate for the lack of VHA-a1 during vegetative growth (Figure 10B and Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area measurements shown in Figure 10B and Figure 10—figure supplement 2.

claim: vha-a1 vha-a2/+ and vha-a1 vha-a3/+ plants both had reduced rosette sizes.
source: Subsequently, vha-a1 (Cas9+) was crossed with vha-a2 and vha-a3 single mutants to determine if both are able to compensate for the lack of VHA-a1. vha-a1 vha-a2/+ and vha-a1 vha-a3/+ plants both had reduced rosette sizes, however the latter showed a stronger reduction which is in accordance with VHA-a3 being expressed at higher levels than VHA-a2 (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by plant images shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 2.

claim: vha-a1 vha-a3/+ showed a stronger reduction in rosette size than vha-a1 vha-a2/+ which is in accordance with VHA-a3 being expressed at higher levels than VHA-a2.
source: Subsequently, vha-a1 (Cas9+) was crossed with vha-a2 and vha-a3 single mutants to determine if both are able to compensate for the lack of VHA-a1. vha-a1 vha-a2/+ and vha-a1 vha-a3/+ plants both had reduced rosette sizes, however the latter showed a stronger reduction which is in accordance with VHA-a3 being expressed at higher levels than VHA-a2 (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between expression levels and phenotype severity.

claim: vha-a1/+ vha-a2/+ vha-a3 was smaller than vha-a1/+ vha-a2 vha-a3/+.
source: To analyze mutants with even lower numbers of VHA-a wildtype alleles vha-a1 (Cas9+) vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ was crossed with the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant. Consistent with the results of the single mutant crosses, vha-a1/+ vha-a2/+ vha-a3 was smaller than vha-a1/+ vha-a2 vha-a3/+.
evidence: This is demonstrated by plant images shown in Figure 10C.

claim: vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3/+ was the smallest mutant found.
source: The smallest plants obtained were vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3/+ (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by plant images shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Neither vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3 nor the homozygous triple mutant vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3 were found, suggesting that they are not viable.
source: Neither did we find vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3 nor the homozygous triple mutant vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3, suggesting that they are not viable.
evidence: This is inferred from the absence of these genotypes in the progeny.

claim: Differential targeting mediated by subunit a evolved independently in the different eukaryotic lineages.
source: Whereas the targeting information is contained in the N-terminus of the Golgi-localized yeast isoform Stv1p (Finnigan et al., 2012), it was shown to be provided by the C-terminal part for some of the 17 isoforms of Paramecium tetraurelia that localize the V-ATPase to at least seven different compartments (Wassmer et al., 2006). Moreover, the targeting motif identified in Stv1p (Finnigan et al., 2012) is neither conserved in plant nor mammalian subunit a isoforms implying that differential targeting mediated by subunit a evolved independently in the different eukaryotic lineages.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of conservation of targeting motifs across different lineages.

claim: Marchantia might represent the ancestral ground state with a single VHA-isoform predominantly localized at the tonoplast.
source: With the exception of Marchantia and Salvina culculatta, all other plants outside of the spermatophytes possess multiple VHA-a isoforms, however the a1-TD is not conserved in these plants. Evidence for differential targeting of VHA-a isoforms is missing but it seems reasonable to speculate that differential localization arose independently. Based on this, Marchantia might represent the ancestral ground state with a single VHA-isoform predominantly localized at the tonoplast.
evidence: This is speculated based on phylogenetic analysis and localization data.

claim: The identity of the VHA-a isoform can influence a number of biochemical properties including assembly, coupling efficiency, protein abundance and reversible dissociation.
source: The identity of the VHA-a isoform does not only determine the subcellular localization, it can influence a number of biochemical properties including assembly, coupling efficiency, protein abundance and reversible dissociation (Leng et al., 1998; Kawasaki-Nishi et al., 2001b, Kawasaki-Nishi et al., 2001a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD which are mislocalized to the tonoplast have retained their basal proton-pumping activity.
source: The fact that VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD which are mislocalized to the tonoplast can complement the dwarf phenotype of the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant to varying degrees argues strongly that they have retained their basal proton-pumping activity and do not require the specific lipid-environment of the TGN/EE for functionality.
evidence: This is inferred from the complementation data shown in Figure 7.

claim: VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD do not require the specific lipid-environment of the TGN/EE for functionality.
source: The fact that VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD which are mislocalized to the tonoplast can complement the dwarf phenotype of the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant to varying degrees argues strongly that they have retained their basal proton-pumping activity and do not require the specific lipid-environment of the TGN/EE for functionality.
evidence: This is inferred from the complementation data shown in Figure 7.

claim: In Arabidopsis, cells that require large quantities of tonoplast membranes such as the cells of the root tip, the VHA-a isoforms compete for entry into COPII vesicles.
source: We propose here that in Arabidopsis, cells that require large quantities of tonoplast membranes such as the cells of the root tip, the VHA-a isoforms compete for entry into COPII vesicles.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claim: The ratio of VHA-a1 to VHA-a3 is roughly 1:10 based on RNA expression and enzymatic activity.
source: Assembly of all VO-complexes takes place at the ER with the help of dedicated assembly factors and based on RNA expression and enzymatic activity the ratio of VHA-a1 to VHA-a3 is roughly 1:10 (Hanitzsch et al., 2007; Neubert et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Due to the presence of the a1-TD, the affinity of VHA-a1 for Sec24, the cargo receptor for COPII vesicles, is much higher than the affinity of VHA-a3.
source: We assume that due to the presence of the a1-TD, the affinity of VHA-a1 for Sec24, the cargo receptor for COPII vesicles, is much higher than the affinity of VHA-a3.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claim: Small quantities of VHA-a3 can enter COPII vesicles but the majority is predominantly sorted into the Golgi-independent route.
source: Small quantities of VHA-a3 can enter COPII vesicles but the majority is predominantly sorted into the Golgi-independent route (Figure 11).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data and illustrated in Figure 11.

claim: In the absence of VHA-a1, VHA-a2/VHA-a3 would be able to enter the COPII-route more efficiently and would thus be able to compensate for the lack of V-ATPases at the TGN/EE.
source: Similarly, in the absence of VHA-a1, VHA-a2/VHA-a3 would be able to enter the COPII-route more efficiently and would thus be able to compensate for the lack of V-ATPases at the TGN/EE providing an explanation for the lack of a vegetative phenotype of the vha-a1 mutant.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claim: In the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant in which VHA-a1 is the only remaining target, treatment with the V-ATPase inhibitor ConcA causes an additional increase in vacuolar pH although the localization of VHA-a1 is not affected.
source: We have shown previously that despite their seemingly strict spatial separation, the activities of the V-ATPase at the TGN/EE and the tonoplast are coordinated. In the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant in which VHA-a1 is the only remaining target, treatment with the V-ATPase inhibitor ConcA causes an additional increase in vacuolar pH (Kriegel et al., 2015) although the localization of VHA-a1 is not affected.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In the RNA-mediated knock-down lines, although levels of VHA-a1 are reduced, they are still sufficient to outcompete VHA-a3 for entry into COPII vesicles.
source: Based on our model, we propose that in the RNA-mediated knock-down lines, although levels of VHA-a1 are reduced, they are still sufficient to outcompete VHA-a3 for entry into COPII vesicles.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.
